senses.gloss: f. pl. (= על־ענקא on the neck) poles used to carry burdens on the shoulder of two or more persons (v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Falangæ, phalangæ, which is of Semitic origin).
units: Bets. 25ᵇ what means ‘provided no carrying on shoulders takes place’? Ans. באלנקי … Ar., Ms. M. (ed. באלו׳) by means of alanke (phalangæ).
<cite ref="Beitzah 25b:14">Ib.</cite> <he>למיפק אאלו׳</he> ed. (Ms. <he>באל׳</he>) to be taken out &c. (carried in a sedan chair through which poles are put).

<cite ref="Beitzah 25b:14">Ib.</cite> Am. and Mar Zut. allowed themselves to be carried on shoulders of men <he>בשבתא דריגלא באלנ׳</he> Ar., Ms. M. (ed. our w. absent) on a Sabbath during the festive week on phalangæ (to the lecture room). V. <cite ref="B00834"><he>בְּלוּנְקֵי</he></cite>.
